products.name: NVIDIA Omniverse
products.one_liner: Modular, agent-ready libraries for building and validating simulation-ready 3D worlds for physical AI.
products.what_it_does: Omniverse is a set of libraries, APIs, and services that developers embed in their existing 3D applications rather than a standalone app. It covers OpenUSD data interoperability, RTX rendering and sensor simulation (ovrtx), GPU physics (ovphysx), and SimReady asset validation. AI agents can call these libraries as tools to prepare content, assemble simulation workflows, and flag issues for review.
products.digital_twin_role: Provides the structured OpenUSD scene, rendering, physics, and sensor simulation used to turn facility and equipment data into simulation-ready digital twins of factories and AI factories, where design and operational changes are tested before implementation.
capabilities: RTX rendering and camera/lidar/radar sensor simulation (ovrtx)
GPU-accelerated physics for motion, contacts, and collisions (ovphysx)
Agent skills callable by frontier AI agents

products.name: NVIDIA Isaac Sim
products.one_liner: Open-source robotics simulation framework for testing robots and generating synthetic data in physically based worlds.
products.what_it_does: Isaac Sim is an open-source, extensible framework for simulating robots and sensors in physically based virtual environments. Developers import CAD, URDF, or real-world captures, convert them to USD, assemble scenes with materials, physics, and robot and sensor models, then generate synthetic data and test full robot stacks.
products.digital_twin_role: It turns CAD and real-world captures into OpenUSD simulation scenes that act as digital twins for training perception and mobility stacks and running software- or hardware-in-the-loop tests.
capabilities: Physically based robot and sensor simulation
Controllable synthetic data generation with annotations
Import from CAD, URDF, MJCF, and real-world captures

products.name: OpenUSD
products.one_liner: Open, extensible scene-description framework that serves as the shared 3D data layer for digital twins and physical AI.
products.what_it_does: OpenUSD (Universal Scene Description), originally created by Pixar, describes and composes 3D content as layered scene descriptions assembled into a single 'stage' of prims. Composition arcs such as references and variant sets let teams reuse and vary assets nondestructively, and the format natively carries physics properties, materials, sensor data, and metadata. Standardization is driven by the Alliance for OpenUSD (AOUSD).
products.digital_twin_role: It acts as the common data layer that merges CAD geometry, materials, simulation physics, and live sensor streams into one queryable, updatable scene for a digital twin. SimReady specifications on top of it define what assets need to be valid for physical AI simulation.
capabilities: Aggregating CAD and BIM data into a common 3D environment
Multi-tool collaboration in one virtual environment
Simulation-ready assets with geometry, materials, and physics properties
Layered, nondestructive scene composition on a single stage
Native physics properties (mass, friction, joints, colliders) in the scene

products.name: NVIDIA Cosmos
products.one_liner: Open platform of world foundation models, datasets, and tools for building physical AI world models.
products.what_it_does: Cosmos provides open world foundation models (the Cosmos 3 Super, Nano, and Edge omni-models) plus datasets, data curation tools, and a training framework for building and specializing world models. The models can reason over video as a VLM, act as a physics-grounded world simulator, generate synthetic data from multimodal inputs, and serve as a backbone for robot world action models.
products.digital_twin_role: Cosmos complements Omniverse simulations: Omniverse renders the simulation environment, and Cosmos Transfer models turn those simulations into controllable, photorealistic synthetic data, while Cosmos itself can run closed-loop world simulation for evaluating physical AI behavior.
capabilities: Reasoning over video as a vision language model

products.name: Newton
products.one_liner: Open-source, extensible GPU physics engine for robot simulation and policy training, built on Warp and OpenUSD.
products.what_it_does: Newton is an open-source physics engine that keeps the physical model, state, controls, contacts, and solver as separate pieces so developers can pick the numerical method that suits their problem. It uses MJWarp as a key rigid-body solver and can be coupled with other solvers, such as a deformable cable solver, for multiphysics tasks.
products.digital_twin_role: It supplies the physics backend for virtual robot environments in Isaac Sim and Isaac Lab, where robot policies are trained and validated before being moved to physical hardware.
capabilities: Modular, selectable solvers including MJWarp for rigid bodies
Coupled multiphysics for deformable objects such as cables

products.name: NVIDIA cuOpt
products.one_liner: Open-source GPU-accelerated decision optimization engine for routing, scheduling, and large-scale mathematical programming.
products.what_it_does: cuOpt is an open-source solver that uses GPUs to tackle optimization problems with millions of variables and constraints, including linear and quadratic programming and vehicle routing, with mixed integer programming in beta. products.digital_twin_role: When integrated with Omniverse digital twins, cuOpt optimizes logistics by simulating real-world fleet operations virtually, supporting dynamic scheduling, route optimization, and predictive planning.
capabilities: GPU-accelerated LP, QP, and vehicle routing solvers
Beta mixed integer programming focused on fast feasible solutions
Dynamic and batch re-optimization in near real time
